failure_patterns.pattern: parameter_mapping_or_canonicalization: Calls omitted, misgrouped, or misrepresented schema fields and constraints, including selectors, filters, locales, pagination, and canonical values.

rejected_edits.content: For news publisher/source filters whose schema expects domain hosts, convert recognized outlet names to canonical lowercase hostnames (for example, CNN to `cnn.com` and BBC to `bbc.com`), then combine multiple outlets using the documented delimiter; do not pass bare or display-name labels when hostnames are expected.
rejected_edits.target: Preserve query values and their entity associations, converting them only to documented formats such as API codes, list syntax, or canonical enum spelling.

rejected_edits.content: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call; do the same where applicable when a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint. For an initial collection retrieval even without an explicit first-page request, use the documented or unambiguous canonical initial position when the endpoint exposes a page/index convention (for example, `page=1` for one-based pages or `start=0`/`offset=0` for zero-based indexes). Do not confuse an offset with a page number or invent a result limit.
rejected_edits.target: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call; do the same where applicable when a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint.

rejected_edits.content: When a request supplies multiple targets or values for a parameter whose schema is scalar, make a separate call for each value, keeping other arguments associated with the appropriate target. Repeat a parameter within one call only when the endpoint explicitly documents repeated values or batch/list encoding; do not treat an undocumented repeated scalar parameter as bulk input.
rejected_edits.target: For multi-value filters, preserve whether the user asks for any listed value or for all of them to match. Use the endpoint's documented list encoding and, when available, its documented match-mode parameter; do not assume comma-separated values or an all-match mode without schema support.
